content.text: The text reviews intestinal obstruction, especially intussusception, stricture, fecal impaction, adhesions, tumors, volvulus, and compression. It describes mechanisms, acute versus chronic symptoms, diagnosis, prognosis, and historical treatments, emphasizing avoidance of purgatives in mechanical obstruction, opium for symptom control, enemas, and timely laparotomy. It then discusses intestinal and rectal cancer, lardaceous degeneration, congenital malformations, prolapse, hemorrhoids, fissures, ulcers, abscesses, fistulae, syphilis, tuberculosis, and related surgical treatments. Extensive sections describe intestinal parasites—including tapeworms, flukes, nematodes, trichinae, and filariae—their life cycles, symptoms, treatment, and prevention. The liver section introduces biliousness and lithaemia. Sandra went back to the bathroom.
